answer: One robust defense is stake-bonded reputation: each agent must lock a small deposit to a single identity thread binding its actions to its bond, so spawning thousands of sock-puppet identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Rather than stopping a gale of new registrations, the economy makes every identity costly and ties trust to how long the bond survives without misbehavior, a surface as hard and testable as polished marble. Peers then route valuable work only to well-bonded identities, starving sybils of revenue.
